content: 1. Trazodone: Mifepristone increases trazodone levels or effects by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Triptorelin and Mifepristone: Triptorelin increases the toxicity of mifepristone by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. Tucatinib and Mifepristone: Mifepristone increases tucatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Concurrent use with CYP3A substrates should be avoided due to the risk of serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate as per product labeling. 4. Ubrogepant: Mifepristone increases ubrogepant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Ulipristal: Mifepristone increases ulipristal levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol: Mifepristone increases the toxicity of this combination by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Exercise caution when co-administering vilanterol with QTc-prolonging drugs. 7. Valbenazine: Mifepristone increases valbenazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Vandetanib: Mifepristone increases vandetanib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Vemurafenib: Mifepristone increases vemurafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Venetoclax: Mifepristone increases venetoclax levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Vilanterol/Fluticasone Furoate: Mifepristone increases the toxicity of this combination by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Voriconazole: Mifepristone increases voriconazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Abemaciclib: Mifepristone increases abemaciclib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Dose adjustments may be necessary if adverse reactions occur. 14. Acalabrutinib: Mifepristone increases acalabrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Limit the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily and monitor for toxicity. 15. Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine: Mifepristone increases the levels of this drug through CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely for adverse reactions. 16. Albuterol: Both mifepristone and albuterol prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 17. Alprazolam: Mifepristone increases alprazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 18. Amiodarone: Mifepristone increases amiodarone levels through CYP2C8/2C9 inhibition. Use the smallest recommended doses and monitor for QT prolongation. 19. Amitriptyline: Both mifepristone and amitriptyline prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Amlodipine: Mifepristone increases amlodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 21. Amobarbital: Amobarbital decreases mifepristone levels by inducing CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 22. Amoxapine: Both mifepristone and amoxapine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Apixaban: Mifepristone increases apixaban levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Apomorphine: Both mifepristone and apomorphine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 25. Aprepitant: Aprepitant increases mifepristone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 26. Arformoterol: Both mifepristone and arformoterol prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Aripiprazole: Mifepristone increases aripiprazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Arsenic Trioxide: Both mifepristone and arsenic trioxide prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Artemether: Both mifepristone and artemether prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Artemether/Lumefantrine: Both mifepristone and this combination prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 31. Asenapine: Both mifepristone and asenapine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Atazanavir: Atazanavir increases mifepristone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Atogepant: Mifepristone increases atogepant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the atogepant dose to 10 mg daily when co-administered. 34. Atomoxetine: Both mifepristone and atomoxetine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 35. Atorvastatin: Mifepristone increases atorvastatin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Do not exceed 40 mg/day of atorvastatin when co-administered. 36. Avatrombopag: Mifepristone increases avatrombopag levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the starting dose of avatrombopag to 20 mg three times weekly when co-administered. 37. Axitinib: Mifepristone increases axitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 38. Azithromycin: Both mifepristone and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Bedaquiline: Both mifepristone and bedaquiline prolong the QTc interval. Avoid concurrent use for more than 14 days unless benefits outweigh risks. 40. Boceprevir: Boceprevir increases mifepristone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome. 41. Bortezomib: Mifepristone increases bortezomib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 42. Bosentan: Bosentan decreases mifepristone levels by inducing CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 43. Brentuximab Vedotin: Mifepristone increases brentuximab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 44. Brexpiprazole: Mifepristone increases brexpiprazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 45. Brigatinib: Mifepristone increases brigatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50% if co-administration is necessary. 46. Bupropion: Mifepristone increases bupropion levels via CYP2B6 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 47. Buspirone: Mifepristone increases buspirone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Start with 5 mg twice daily and adjust based on clinical response. 48. Cabozantinib: Mifepristone increases cabozantinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the cabozantinib dose if co-administration is necessary. 49. Calcifediol: Mifepristone increases calcifediol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 50. Cannabidiol: Mifepristone increases cannabidiol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered. This list continues with similar interactions for other drugs. Each interaction involves either an increase in drug levels or effects due to CYP3A4 inhibition, QTc prolongation, or other mechanisms. In most cases, therapy modification, close monitoring, or alternative drugs are recommended.
